{
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "goal_domain", "analytical_usefulness": 0.35, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Well-grounded from description/category, but appears redundant with the existing 'category' column (values mirror it), reducing new analytical leverage.", "hallucination_observed": false},
    {"name": "management_lever_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Captures the practice/lever used to pursue goals, a genuine grouping axis directly relevant to comparing top-performer practices. Values are sound readings of the described mechanisms."},
    {"name": "target_improvement_magnitude", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Quantifies target ambition, directly relevant to 'how much achievement would improve.' Grounded where percentages stated, but the coarse integer coding (nearly all '3') is opaque and near-constant, limiting leverage and traceability."},
    {"name": "mechanism_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Grounded, but heavily overlaps with management_lever_type (shares values like people_engagement, market_expansion, process_automation), making it largely a restatement of another added column."},
    {"name": "quantified_specificity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.05, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "Constant 'true' across all 550 rows; a near-constant flag provides no grouping or modeling leverage even though it is a fair reading of the specific targets."},
    {"name": "baseline_context_provided", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.65, "rationale": "Presence of a stated baseline (e.g., 'from 78% to 90%') is a real practice differentiator useful for the query. However sample groundedness is shaky: the meeting-time and engagement-program rows lack numeric baselines yet coding is inconsistent (one 'from 75% to 85%' row marked False)."},
    {"name": "has_feedback_loop", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "A meaningful practice axis, but most descriptions do not explicitly mention feedback loops; 'true' assignments risk inference beyond the text. Samples all False, plausible, but broader groundedness uncertain."},
    {"name": "involves_stakeholder_engagement", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Relevant practice dimension. Some inferences are defensible (after-sales support, engagement program) but the sample coding is inconsistent (customer-personalization row marked False, status-meeting row marked True), signaling loose grounding."},
    {"name": "implementation_feasibility_signal", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.45, "rationale": "Feasibility/barrier is highly relevant to estimating achievable improvement, but the source texts rarely state difficulty; barrier levels appear to be model-imposed judgments not clearly warranted by the text."},
    {"name": "implementation_scope", "analytical_usefulness": 0.65, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "rationale": "Scope is a useful axis, but assignments are often not textually supported (e.g., status-meeting goal labeled 'organization_wide', cost goal 'function_specific') and read as guesses where text is silent on scope."},
    {"name": "outcome_metric_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Useful normalized metric axis, but partly redundant with the existing 'metric' column; notably the augmentation sometimes derives from description rather than the (mismatched) metric field, which is reasonable but overlaps existing data."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
  "source_groundedness": 0.68,
  "rationale": "The set offers several genuinely useful practice-differentiating axes (management_lever_type, target_improvement_magnitude, baseline_context_provided, stakeholder/feedback flags) well suited to comparing top-performer goal-management practices. Weaknesses: quantified_specificity is a constant dead flag; goal_domain and mechanism_type are largely redundant with category and each other; and several inferential columns (implementation_feasibility_signal, implementation_scope, feedback/stakeholder flags) assert specifics the terse descriptions do not clearly support, with visible coding inconsistencies across the samples. Overall moderately useful with mixed groundedness."
}
